  <p class="display hero-display"><span class="ln">Everyone counts</span> <span class="ln">on you. Somewhere</span> <span class="ln">in all of it, you lost</span> <span class="ln">track of yourself.</span></p>
  <h1 class="hero-h1">Online IFS and somatic therapy for high-achieving women in San Francisco and across California who are dealing with anxiety, betrayal or burnout, and who give far more than they keep.</h1>
  <div class="hero-links">
    <a class="link link-lg" href="/new-contact">Book a free 30-minute consult</a>
    <a class="link" href="#doors">What we work on</a>
  </div>

<section class="familiar fe">
  <h2 class="fam-h">This has all become too familiar.</h2>
  <figure class="fam-art story"><img class="art" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/line-woman.svg" alt="" width="346" height="412"><figcaption class="cap">knotted</figcaption></figure>
  <ul class="fam-list">
    <li>You're the one people call. You remember the birthdays, fix the problem, and say yes before anyone finishes asking.</li>
    <li>At work you carry more than your share, and you'd rather stay late than let anyone see you struggle.</li>
    <li>You found out about an affair, a secret, or a partner who suddenly wants to open the relationship, and now you question everything you thought you knew.</li>
    <li>You're successful and capable, and your mind still won't stop racing.</li>
    <li>Saying no makes you feel guilty. Saying yes is wearing you down.</li>
    <li>If someone asked what you want, for yourself, you're not sure you'd have an answer.</li>
  </ul>
  <div class="fam-close">
    <p>If you're exceptionally good at showing up for everyone else and somewhere along the way lost touch with yourself, you're in the right place. I help high-achieving women move through anxiety, betrayal and burnout, break free from patterns of overgiving, and build relationships and careers that fulfill them, without losing themselves.</p>
    <a class="link" href="/new-contact">Contact Kristina</a>
  </div>
</section>

      <div><b>9:00</b>Standup</div><div><b>10:00</b>Budget review</div><div><b>11:00</b>Client call</div>

  <div class="ev-copy">
  <h2 class="ev-h">Therapy that fits a full workday.</h2>
  <div class="ev-body">
    <p>Sessions happen by secure video. There's no office to drive to and no waiting room, so an hour of therapy takes an hour, not half your afternoon.</p>
    <p>Plenty of clients log on from a closed office door or a parked car between meetings. You come back to your day a little steadier than you left it.</p>
  </div>
  </div>
  <div class="ev-ca">
    <h2 class="ev-ca-h">Online therapy across California</h2>
    <p class="ev-ca-sub">You can be anywhere in the state. Most of my clients are in San Francisco and around the Bay. <a class="link" href="/new-online-therapy-san-francisco" style="color:#F1F3EF">Online therapy in the Bay Area</a></p>

</section>

<section class="work fe" id="doors">
  <div class="wk-head">
  <h2>Three ways in. One thing we're working toward.</h2>
  <p class="wk-intro">The women I see are leaders, partners and mothers who look fine from the outside. They usually come in through one of these doors.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="doors">
    <a class="door" href="/new-overgiving-in-relationships"><figure><img class="reveal" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/sun-rays-900.webp" alt="Sun breaking through a green forest canopy" loading="lazy"></figure><div class="db"><span class="n">01</span><h3>Overgiving in relationships</h3><p>People-pleasing, a hard time with boundaries, and caring for everyone so well that there's nothing left over for you.</p><span class="go"><span>Overgiving in relationships</span></span></div></a>
    <a class="door" href="/new-betrayalandinfidelity"><figure><img class="reveal" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/redwood-trunks-900.webp" alt="Light falling between tall redwood trunks" loading="lazy"></figure><div class="db"><span class="n">02</span><h3>Betrayal and disclosure trauma</h3><p>An affair, a sexual secret, or a partner who asks out of nowhere to open the marriage. The shock first, then what you want next.</p><span class="go"><span>Betrayal and disclosure trauma</span></span></div></a>
    <a class="door" href="/new-overgiving-at-work"><figure><img class="reveal" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/fern-light-900.webp" alt="Morning light over ferns in a quiet forest" loading="lazy"></figure><div class="db"><span class="n">03</span><h3>Overgiving at work</h3><p>High-functioning anxiety, perfectionism, feeling responsible for everything, and the burnout that comes with being the capable one.</p><span class="go"><span>Overgiving at work</span></span></div></a>
  </div>
  <div class="house"><p>Whichever door you come through, the work is the same: finding yourself again, with your confidence, your clarity and your trust in yourself back.</p><a class="link" href="/new-contact">Book a free consult</a></div>
  <div class="svcs">
    <h3 class="small">How we work</h3>
    <div class="svc-row">
      <a href="/new-ifstherapy"><span>Primary approach</span><h3>IFS therapy</h3><p>Internal Family Systems, blended with somatic work and Brainspotting.</p></a>
      <a href="/new-ifs-intensives"><span>Go deeper, faster</span><h3>IFS intensives</h3><p>Three to four hours of focused work in one sitting, from $1,000.</p></a>
      <a href="/new-kap"><span>When you feel stuck</span><h3>Ketamine-assisted therapy</h3><p>Oral ketamine paired with IFS, through Journey Clinical.</p></a>
      <a href="/new-consultation-for-therapists"><span>For clinicians</span><h3>Consultation for therapists</h3><p>IFS and KAP consultation for newer and growing therapists.</p></a>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="begin fe">
  <h2 class="bg-h" style="position:relative;z-index:2">How we start</h2>
  <figure class="bg-thread story"><img class="draw-in art" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/line-thread.svg" alt="" width="520" height="242" loading="lazy"><figcaption class="cap">unwinding</figcaption></figure>

    <div class="step"><span class="n">First</span><h3>Book a free consult</h3><p>Thirty minutes on video. It isn't a sales call. You'll leave with more clarity about what's going on, whether or not we work together.</p></div>
    <div class="step"><span class="n">Then</span><h3>Meet weekly</h3><p>Sixty to 75 minutes online, using IFS and somatic work, at a time that fits around your day.</p></div>
    <div class="step"><span class="n">Over time</span><h3>Feel it hold</h3><p>You notice it in your body, at work, and in how you show up with the people you love. Some clients stay for ongoing support. Others come back as needed.</p></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="about fe">
  <figure class="ab-photo"><img class="reveal" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/kristina-field.webp" alt="Kristina Shimokawa standing in a sunlit field" width="1500" height="1000" loading="lazy"></figure>
  <div class="ab-text">
    <h2>Hi, I'm Kristina.</h2>
    <p>I'm a therapist, wife and mother, and I know what it's like to look fine on the outside while struggling on the inside. For years I was the overgiver: anxious, people-pleasing, good at everything except trusting myself.</p>
    <p>IFS and Brainspotting changed that for me. Now I use them, along with somatic and attachment-based work, to help women get their footing back.</p>
    <p><a class="link" href="/new-meetkristina">Meet Kristina</a></p>
  </div>

<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>Why I do this work</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>For a long time I was the woman who showed up for everyone. I worked hard, said yes, and kept the anxiety quiet enough that nobody noticed. Inside it was a different story: crippling worry, people-pleasing on autopilot, and very little trust in my own judgment.</p>
    <p>Internal Family Systems therapy and Brainspotting are what finally moved it. They helped me understand the parts of me that were working so hard, and they helped me feel it in my body, not just think about it.</p>
    <p>Now I work with high-achieving women who are going through some version of that. Some are giving too much in their relationships. Some just found out about an affair or a secret that changed everything. Some are burning out at work while everyone assumes they're fine. What they share is that they've lost touch with themselves, and they want back their confidence, their clarity and their trust in their own instincts.</p>
    <p>I believe the mind, body and spirit are all sources of healing. My work blends clinical psychology with somatic techniques and a lot of attention to relationships.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap">
  <h2>How I work</h2>
  <p class="intro-p">Warm, collaborative, zero judgment, and more than talking.</p>
  <div class="two" style="margin-top:46px"><div></div><ol class="numlist"><li><div><b>We go deeper.</b>The topics you don't even tell your closest friends are welcome here: hurt, rage, shame, desire, money, sex, the uncensored thoughts. Nothing is off-limits.</div></li><li><div><b>We work together, not on my agenda.</b>No unsolicited advice and no homework. We move at your pace toward what feels right and true for you.</div></li><li><div><b>We work with your mind and your body.</b>I blend IFS, Brainspotting, and somatic and attachment-based therapy, so you get past insight to real change. For anyone feeling extra stuck, ketamine-assisted therapy is an option when it's clinically appropriate.</div></li><li><div><b>You can show up exactly as you are.</b>You don't have to explain away, minimize or justify what you feel.</div></li><li><div><b>We meet for as long as it helps.</b>Usually weekly, until you feel real resolution. Some clients stay for ongoing support. Others come back when they need to. It doesn't have to be forever.</div></li><li><div><b>We build communication skills.</b>Very few of us were taught how to say what we need. We practice it in individual sessions, with brief couples sessions as an option.</div></li></ol></div>
</div></section>

Who takes care of you?</h1><p class="lede">Online therapy for women in San Francisco and across California who are people-pleasing, caught in codependent patterns, struggling with boundaries, and disappearing a little more each time they put someone else first.</p><div class="hero-links"><a class="link link-lg" href="/new-contact">Book a free 30-minute consult</a></div></div><figure><span class="arch" aria-hidden="true"></span><img class="arch-img" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/sun-rays-900.webp" alt="Sun breaking through a green forest canopy"></figure></div></section>
<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap">
  <h2>Does any of this sound like you?</h2>
  <div style="margin-top:40px"><ul class="ticks"><li>You agree before you've even checked how you feel about it.</li><li>Someone else's bad mood becomes your problem to fix.</li><li>You rehearse hard conversations for days, then don't have them.</li><li>You feel guilty resting while anyone around you still needs something.</li><li>Your partner, kids, parents and friends all get the best of you. You get what's left.</li><li>Setting a boundary feels mean, even when you know it isn't.</li><li>You attract people who take, and you keep giving anyway.</li><li>Your mood rises and falls with how the people you love are doing.</li><li>You're not sure who you are when nobody needs you.</li></ul></div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>People-pleasing started as protection.</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Most overgivers learned it early. Keeping the peace, reading the room and being the easy one kept you safe, or loved, or out of trouble. That part of you did its job well.</p>
    <p>The trouble is it never got the message that you grew up. It still runs the show in your marriage, your friendships and your family, and it costs you your own needs, your voice and a lot of quiet resentment.</p>
    <p>In IFS therapy we don't try to shut that part down. We get to know it, find out what it's afraid would happen if it stopped, and help it trust that you can handle things now. When it relaxes, there's room for you.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>

</div><section class="ph-hero dark"><div class="wrap"><div><p class="eyebrow">Betrayal and disclosure trauma</p><h1>Something happened that changed your relationship overnight.</h1><p class="lede">Online therapy for high-achieving women in the Bay Area and across California after infidelity, a sexual secret, or a partner who suddenly wants to open the relationship.</p><div class="hero-links"><a class="link link-lg" href="/new-contact">Book a free 30-minute consult</a></div></div><figure><span class="arch" aria-hidden="true"></span><img class="arch-img" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/redwood-trunks-1600.webp" alt="Light falling between tall redwood trunks" style="aspect-ratio:4/5"></figure></div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>Your relationship once felt trusting and close.</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Then you found the messages, or heard the confession, or listened to your partner ask for something you never signed up for. Now everything feels unsettled, and you don't know what's supposed to happen next.</p>
    <p>You've replayed every conversation and searched for an explanation that finally makes it make sense. You love your partner, and you also don't know if you can stay. Maybe you're carrying a story you haven't told anyone, because it feels too painful, too complicated or too taboo, and you're afraid of how people would judge you, or them.</p>
    <p>What usually follows is a mix of anxiety, grief and uncertainty that's hard to explain to anyone. You don't have to carry it alone, and you don't have to decide anything today.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec spruce"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>Maybe you're asking yourself</h2><p class="intro-p">None of these have simple answers. That's what our time together is for.</p></div>
  <ul class="qs"><li>Can I stay?</li><li>Can I ever trust again?</li><li>Am I asking for too much?</li><li>What do I actually want?</li></ul>
</div></section>
<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap">
  <h2>How we work through it</h2>
  <ol class="tl">
    <li><span>First</span><h3>Steady the shock</h3><p>Betrayal hits the body before the mind catches up: sleepless nights, racing thoughts, a stomach that won't settle. We start by helping your nervous system come down enough to think.</p></li>
    <li><span>Then</span><h3>Make sense of it</h3><p>With IFS we get to know the parts of you that are furious, heartbroken, numb or desperate for answers. Each one has something to say about what you need.</p></li>
    <li><span>Over time</span><h3>Decide from a clear place</h3><p>Staying, leaving, or something in between. You get to choose from your own clarity, not from panic or pressure.</p></li>
  </ol>
  <p class="note">Individual IFS and somatic therapy are the core of this work. Brief couples sessions are an option when you want support with your partner.</p>
</div></section>

<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>High-functioning anxiety looks a lot like success.</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>You're the one people rely on. You hit the deadline, catch the mistake, cover for the colleague and still answer email at 10 PM. From the outside it looks like ambition. From the inside it feels like you can't afford to stop.</p>
    <p>The worry never fully shuts off. Praise doesn't land for long. A small piece of criticism can take up your whole weekend. And the exhaustion is getting harder to push through.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap">
  <h2>You might notice</h2>
  <div style="margin-top:40px"><ul class="ticks"><li>A constant hum of worry, even when things are going well</li><li>Perfectionism and a harsh inner critic</li><li>Feeling responsible for outcomes that aren't yours to carry</li><li>Trouble delegating because it's faster to do it yourself</li><li>Imposter feelings no promotion seems to fix</li><li>A tight chest, clenched jaw or racing heart at the end of the day</li><li>Sleep that doesn't feel restful</li><li>Saying yes to more work while dreading all of it</li></ul></div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec spruce"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>What we do about it</h2></div>
  <div><ol class="numlist"><li><div><b>Get to know the driver.</b>The part of you that pushes so hard usually believes something bad will happen if it lets up. In IFS we find out what it's protecting, so it doesn't have to work this hard.</div></li><li><div><b>Settle your body.</b>Anxiety lives in the body. We use somatic tools to notice it early and help your nervous system shift out of constant alert.</div></li><li><div><b>Soften the critic.</b>Instead of arguing with your inner critic, we listen to it. Critics tend to quiet down once they feel heard.</div></li><li><div><b>Go faster, if you want.</b>IFS intensives of up to four hours can do the work of weeks of weekly sessions. Ask about them in your consult.</div></li></ol></div>
</div></section>

  <div class="prose"><p>Sessions are online, so there's nothing to drive to. Many clients log on from a closed office door or a parked car between meetings, then go back to their day a little lighter.</p><p><a href="/new-therapyoptionsandfees">See session options and fees</a></p></div>

<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>You've tried coping. You want to understand.</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Maybe you've done therapy before and it focused on short-term tools. They helped for a while. But the worry kept coming back, and the voice of self-doubt never really stopped.</p>
    <p>IFS works differently. Instead of managing symptoms, it helps you understand why you feel the way you do, and change the patterns underneath.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>What are parts?</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Have you ever said something like, "Part of me is nervous, but part of me is excited"? That's the idea. We all have inner parts, different sides of us that each try to help in their own way.</p>
    <p>Some parts protect you by planning, pleasing, criticizing or staying busy. Others carry old hurt. Underneath them is what IFS calls the Self: the calm, curious, compassionate you that's still there even when the parts are loud.</p>
    <p>In IFS we don't push parts away. We listen to them. As they feel understood, they relax, and you get more access to your own clarity.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<div class="band" aria-hidden="true"><img src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/soft-forest-1600.webp" alt="" loading="lazy"></div>

    <li><span>Slow down</span><h3>Turn your attention inward</h3><p>We notice what shows up as thoughts, feelings or sensations in your body. It can feel a lot like an active meditation.</p></li>
    <li><span>Get curious</span><h3>Meet the part</h3><p>Instead of fighting the anxiety or the critic, we ask what it's doing for you and what it's afraid of.</p></li>
    <li><span>Let it settle</span><h3>Help it relax</h3><p>When a part feels heard, it stops working so hard. You walk out calmer, clearer and more grounded.</p></li>
  </ol>

</div><section class="ph-hero wide"><div class="wrap"><div><p class="eyebrow">Ketamine-assisted psychotherapy</p><h1>When talk therapy has helped, but not enough.</h1><p class="lede">Online ketamine-assisted therapy (KAP) in the Bay Area and across California for treatment-resistant anxiety, depression and trauma. Paired with IFS for deeper healing.</p><div class="hero-links"><a class="link link-lg" href="/new-contact">Book a free 30-minute consult</a></div></div><figure><img class="" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/redwood-mist-1600.webp" alt="Sunlight through a misty redwood forest"></figure></div></section>
<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>The problem isn't you or your effort.</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>The therapy you've done gave you insight and tools. But the anxiety, depression or effects of trauma are still there. Many people who reach this point have already worked very hard to feel different.</p>
    <p>Sometimes healing takes a shift in perspective that lets the brain and nervous system see things in a new way. Ketamine-assisted therapy can help create that shift.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>How KAP works</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>KAP combines ketamine treatment with psychotherapy. Ketamine can temporarily increase neuroplasticity, which makes the brain and nervous system more open to new perspectives and emotional processing.</p>
    <p>With skilled support, that openness can lead to insight, compassion and change that's hard to reach through talking alone. I pair it with IFS, so the experience connects to the parts work we're already doing.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap">
  <h2>The KAP process</h2>
  <p class="intro-p">One round is preparation, medicine and integration: about five hours of therapy across one week.</p>
  <ol class="tl">
    <li><span>Step 1</span><h3>Free consultation</h3><p>We talk about whether KAP is the right fit. You'll need to be in therapy with me already, or complete four sessions first.</p></li>
    <li><span>Step 2</span><h3>Medical and psychiatric assessment</h3><p>I partner with Journey Clinical, who handle the assessment and prescription. Their fee is separate.</p></li>
    <li><span>Step 3</span><h3>Preparation</h3><p>One to four 50-minute sessions that combine IFS with KAP preparation, so you go in with a clear intention. Online medicine sessions require a chaperone with you.</p></li>
    <li><span>Step 4</span><h3>Medicine session</h3><p>Two to three hours: grounding, meditation, the sublingual ketamine, the experience itself, and coming back into your body.</p></li>
    <li><span>Step 5</span><h3>Integration</h3><p>A 50 to 80 minute session where we make meaning of what came up and choose small steps toward change.</p></li>
  </ol>
  <p class="note">$1,500 per round. Four to six rounds are typically recommended. Fees don't include the assessment with the prescriber or the cost of the medication.</p>
</div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap two even">
  <div><h2>With respect for the original practitioners</h2></div>
  <div class="prose"><p>Many Indigenous cultures have long relationships with plant medicines and altered states for healing and insight. I hold deep respect for those traditions and recognize them as the original practitioners of this work.</p><p>Ketamine is a pharmaceutical medicine. Used sublingually in a therapeutic setting, it can create a gentler, less clinical experience that still supports meaningful healing.</p></div>
</div></section>

<section class="sec" style="padding-top:0"><div class="wrap two"><div></div><div class="faq">
  <h2>Getting started</h2>
  <details><summary>Where are you located?</summary><div><p>I live and work on Maui, and I see clients online anywhere in California. I'm also licensed in Hawaii.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>Do you offer in-person sessions?</summary><div><p>Not at this time. All sessions happen by secure video.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>What happens in the free consult?</summary><div><p>It's 30 minutes on video. You tell me a little about what's going on, ask anything you want, and we see whether working together feels like a good fit. There's no pressure either way.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>What can I expect in my first session?</summary><div><p>Your first session is a little different from the weekly ones. I'll ask about your history (you'll fill out an online intake form beforehand), we'll set your goals, and we'll start building trust and safety.</p></div></details>
  <h2>Fees and insurance</h2>
  <details><summary>What are your fees?</summary><div><p>Weekly sessions are $300 for 60 to 75 minutes. IFS intensives start at $1,000. A round of KAP (preparation, medicine and integration) is $1,500. See <a href="/new-therapyoptionsandfees">fees</a> for details.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>Do you take insurance?</summary><div><p>I'm an out-of-network provider. I can give you a superbill to submit for possible reimbursement, depending on your plan.</p><p>A superbill requires a mental health diagnosis that goes into your medical record. Many people prefer the privacy of paying directly.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>Can I use my FSA or HSA?</summary><div><p>Yes. I accept all major credit cards, including FSA and HSA cards.</p></div></details>
  <h2>How I work</h2>
  <details><summary>What kind of therapy do you do?</summary><div><p>Mostly Internal Family Systems (IFS), a gentle, evidence-informed approach that blends parts work, nervous system healing and mindfulness. When it helps, I add Brainspotting, a somatic therapy that uses eye position to process experiences held in the body. For clients who haven't found lasting change in traditional therapy, I also offer ketamine-assisted psychotherapy.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>Do you see couples?</summary><div><p>My work is individual therapy. Brief couples sessions are available as an add-on when you want support with your partner.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>Do you work with men or LGBTQ+ clients?</summary><div><p>Yes. I welcome and affirm clients of all gender identities and expressions. As a cisgender woman, I know fit matters, especially for clients whose identity differs from mine. I have experience with diverse clients, though I don't present myself as an expert. Anyone who feels safe working with me is welcome.</p></div></details>
  <details><summary>How long does therapy take?</summary><div><p>We usually meet weekly until you feel real resolution. Some people stay for ongoing support, and others come back as needed. It doesn't have to be forever.</p></div></details>
</div></div></section>

<p>This policy explains what information journeywithkristina.com collects and how it is used. It covers the website only. Your clinical records are protected separately under HIPAA, as described in the Notice of Privacy Practices you receive when therapy begins.</p>
<h2>What I collect</h2>
<ul><li><b>Information you send me.</b> When you use the contact form or email me, I receive what you include, such as your name, email, phone number and message.</li>
<li><b>Basic site analytics.</b> The site runs on Squarespace, which collects standard information like pages visited, browser type and approximate location to produce visitor statistics.</li>
<li><b>Cookies.</b> Squarespace uses cookies to make the site work and to measure traffic. You can manage cookies in your browser settings.</li></ul>
<h2>How it's used</h2>
<p>I use your contact information only to reply to you and to schedule a consultation. I don't sell, rent or trade it, and I don't add you to a mailing list unless you ask.</p>
<h2>Keep it brief</h2>
<p>Website forms and regular email are not a secure way to share health information. Please keep your first message short. We can talk about details in a confidential session.</p>
<h2>Third-party services</h2>
<p>The site uses Squarespace for hosting, forms and analytics. Payments and session records are handled through a separate, secure telehealth platform once we begin working together. Each of these services has its own privacy policy.</p>
<h2>Your choices</h2>
<p>You can ask me to delete any messages you've sent through the site by emailing <a href="mailto:kshimokawa.lmft@gmail.com">kshimokawa.lmft@gmail.com</a>. California residents have additional rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act, and I'm happy to help with any request.</p>
<h2>Changes</h2>
<p>If this policy changes, the date at the top will be updated.</p></div></div></section><div class="mbar" id="mbar"><span class="mbar-t">Free 30-minute consult</span><a href="/new-contact">Book now</a></div>

We go straight to the root of the pattern instead of starting and stopping every week.</p><div class="hero-links"><a class="link link-lg" href="/new-contact">Book a free 30-minute consult</a></div></div><figure><img class="" src="https://therapistweb.design/work/preview/journey-with-kristina/img/redwood-band-1600.webp" alt="Sunlight across a quiet redwood forest"></figure></div></section>
<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>Why one long session works</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>In a weekly hour, a lot of the time goes to settling in and catching up, and just when things get real, the session ends. An intensive gives your system enough time to slow down, get underneath the protective parts, and actually finish something.</p>
    <p>Many clients say one intensive feels like weeks, even months, of weekly therapy. We use somatic IFS to shift the pattern at its root, not just talk about it.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec"><div class="wrap">
  <h2>An intensive might fit if</h2>
  <div style="margin-top:40px"><ul class="ticks"><li>Your calendar makes weekly therapy hard to keep up</li><li>You've done years of talk therapy and want to get past insight</li><li>You're in the middle of a betrayal or a big decision and need room to think</li><li>One pattern keeps running your life, and you're ready to work on it directly</li><li>You're already in weekly therapy and want a deeper push</li><li>You'd rather do focused work now than spread it over months</li></ul></div>
</div></section>
<section class="sec spruce"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>How it works</h2></div>
  <div><ol class="numlist"><li><div><b>Free consult first.</b>We talk through what you want to work on and whether an intensive makes sense for you right now.</div></li><li><div><b>One focused session.</b>Three to four hours online, with breaks, using IFS and somatic work.</div></li><li><div><b>Then, what helps next.</b>Some clients add weekly sessions afterward. Others come back for another intensive when they're ready.</div></li></ol></div>
</div></section>

<section class="sec mist"><div class="wrap two">
  <div><h2>Bay Area life doesn't leave much room</h2></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Long commutes, demanding jobs, and a cost of living that keeps everyone running. Many of the women I work with in the Bay are leading teams, raising kids, and holding a relationship together, often all at once.</p>
    <p>Online therapy takes the drive out of it. You log on from your office, your car or your living room, and you're back to your day an hour later.</p>
  </div>
</div></section>

    <a href="/new-betrayalandinfidelity"><span>Specialty</span><h3>Betrayal and disclosure trauma</h3><p>Infidelity, sexual secrets, or a sudden request to open the relationship.</p></a>
